name: Bitrix24
tagline: A sprawling business suite: CRM, tasks, chat, telephony, documents, HR and a site builder in one login.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Bitrix24 has a free tier and several paid team plans billed flat for a user bundle.

verdictSummary: Bitrix24 is not one app, it is about a dozen stapled together: CRM pipelines, task boards, group chat, video calls, a telephony stack with call recording, document storage, e-signature, HR absence tracking and a drag and drop website builder. You can one-shot any single slice of that, and a solo contacts plus deals plus tasks tracker is genuinely an afternoon. What you cannot one-shot is the part people actually buy, which is one login where the whole team lives and every record links to every other record. The telephony and the inbound channel connectors are vendor relationships, not code. Nobody runs Bitrix24 alone, so a personal replacement is answering a question the product was not asked.
coreLoopDIY: A local CRM and task tracker where contacts, deals and to-dos share one SQLite database and one list view.
requirements: Local disk for the SQLite file
Nothing else, no accounts, no cloud
whatYouLose: Telephony: inbound and outbound calls, call recording, IVR, click to dial from a contact record
Shared workspace: permissions, roles, who-saw-what, activity streams, @mentions
Inbound channels: web forms, WhatsApp, email and social messages landing in the same inbox as the CRM record
Mobile apps that actually sync, plus desktop chat clients
Everything outside CRM: documents, e-signature, HR absence calendars, the website and store builder
moatNotes: The telephony and messaging channel integrations are the real lock. Once a company's phone numbers and WhatsApp line route into Bitrix24, leaving means a migration project, not an export.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is five subscriptions and a glue layer. Bitrix24 is bought by small teams who want CRM, chat, tasks and a phone system on one invoice, usually at a price that undercuts buying those separately, and the free tier gets them in the door before the data makes leaving expensive. The suite is not the best version of any single module and most buyers know it. They pay for one login, one admin panel and one vendor to shout at, which is a real thing software cannot replace for you.
notes: The CRM table is a weekend build; the phone system and the shared inbox are not. The moat is being the single login a whole team already routes its calls, messages and permissions through.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user CRM and task tracker called "Desk". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/desk.db, created on first run
- Server actions for all writes, no separate API layer
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, nothing else

Data model:
- contacts: id, name, company, email, phone, notes, created_at
- deals: id, contact_id, title, value_cents, currency, stage (lead | qualified | proposal | won | lost), expected_close, notes, updated_at
- tasks: id, title, due_date, done (0/1), contact_id nullable, deal_id nullable, notes
- activity: id, contact_id, kind (call | email | meeting | note), body, happened_at

Screens:
1. /contacts: searchable table, click through to a contact page showing their deals, open tasks and activity log, with an inline "log activity" form
2. /pipeline: kanban columns by deal stage, drag to move stage, column headers show count and summed value
3. /tasks: one list, overdue first, then today, then upcoming, then done collapsed. Inline add, checkbox to complete
4. /: a dashboard with open deal value, tasks due today, and the five most recent activity entries

Also:
- Seed the database with 8 fake contacts and 6 deals across stages on first run
- A /export route that dumps every table to JSON so the data is never trapped
- A single `npm run backup` script that copies the SQLite file with a timestamp

Explicitly out of scope: authentication, multi user, permissions, email sending, telephony, chat, file storage, calendar sync, mobile apps. Do not add them, do not stub them.

Write a README with setup in under ten lines and one paragraph naming what this deliberately does not do.
